newsitem.title: USA: Federal-Mogul to sell bearings operations.
newsitem.headline: Federal-Mogul to sell bearings operations.

text.p: Federal-Mogul Corp. said Tuesday it will sell its heavy-wall bearing operations in Germany and Brazil to Zollern BHW Gleitlager GmbH, part of Fuerstlich Hohenzollernsche Werke Laucherthal GmbH & Co.
Federal-Mogul, an auto parts maker, did not disclose terms of the deal.

The sale includes the Braunschweiger Huettenwerk GmbH subsidiary, with facilities in Braunschweig and Wildemann, Germany, and the Glyco do Brasil Industria Metalurgica Limitada subsidiary in Cataguasas, Brazil, Federal-Mogul said.

The heavy-wall bearing operations employ about 425 workers in Germany and 140 in Brazil in the manufacture of bearings for large diesel engines, gears and general industrial machinery, Federal-Mogul said.
Founded in 1708, Zollern's primary business areas include casting technology, steel profile, mechanical components, gears and winches.

"The sale of this non-core business will complete our divestiture plans for manufacturing operations," said Richard Snell, chief executive of Federal-Mogul. "This will allow Federal-Mogul management to focus attention and resources on being a valued manufacturer and distributor of automotive and truck parts to both our original equipment and aftermarket customers."
The sale is expected to be close in 30 days, it said.
Federal-Mogul's stock was unchanged at $22.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
